What we can prove, and what we are estimating

The headline materials

How these numbers were built

1 · Start from what we sold

Every confirmed order line for the two years to 31 July 2026. Freight, labour and testing are stripped out.

2 · Run it through the recipe

The bill of materials for the exact product sold, expanded recursively through intermediates until only bought-in raws remain.

3 · Check it balances

A product cannot contain more raw material than it weighs. Anything that fails falls back to the master production workbook, or is set aside.

Read this before quoting a number

This is consumption driven by sales, not purchases. It excludes stock movement, wastage, samples and internal use, and it does not cover the custom prescription blends we mix to order — those are listed separately rather than spread across the materials, so nothing here is inflated by guesswork.

Liquids are reported in litres and solids in kilograms, the units they are bought in. They are never added together. Water and packaging are tracked but kept out of the headline, since neither is bought from a fertiliser supplier.

Coverage & method

How far the numbers can be pushed.

What each confidence tier means, what is deliberately not attributed, and the checks the model has to pass before it is published.

Confidence tiers

Not attributed to a recipe

Real sales with no reliable recipe behind them — mostly one-off prescription blends mixed to a customer's specification. Listed here rather than spread across the materials above. This doubles as the work queue: entering a bill of materials for the largest of these lifts coverage most.

Adjustments and checks

Known soft spots

Carbon Granule is the largest single line and is probably still overstated. It comes almost entirely from Pearl Surge and Pearl Array bulk sales. Worth an eyeball before it is quoted.

Archived bills of material in the ERP are not reliable — several record tonnes where they mean kilograms. The mass-balance check catches the result, but the underlying records need fixing.

Packaging

Split out of the bill of materials tree and excluded from raw material totals.
